title: Cap. IV Arg. 2 Sol: Apostle twisted — faith here actual, not foreseen; Enoch walked with God
pass_a_gloss: Solution. To the Apostle's words themselves we first answer, That they are twisted most badly, and into a sense wholly alien from the Apostolic purpose. For faith in this place shows not the foreseen faith of a man not yet existing, but actual faith, and already exercising its powers. This is clear from that other word εὐηρέστησεν, To please, which the Apostle borrowed from the version of the Seventy Interpreters. For so they at Gen. 5:24, Enoch pleased God. But in the Hebrew it is had, he walked continually with God: that is, He did not imitate the wickedness of his age, but with a sincere heart continually served God, and purely worshiped God. The Apostle therefore willed to say nothing else than that no one can lead a pious life pleasing to God without faith; which he willed to confirm by the example of Enoch. Of wondrous genius therefore are the Remonstrants, who were able to carve out from here their election hanging from foresight of faith.
pass_b_english: Sol. First to the Apostle's words: they are twisted badly into a sense wholly alien to his purpose. Faith here is not the foreseen faith of a man not yet existing, but actual faith already at work. That is clear from εὐηρέστησεν, to please — which Paul takes from the LXX at Gen. 5:24, Enoch pleased God; the Hebrew is he walked continually with God — he did not imitate his age's wickedness but served God sincerely and worshiped him purely. So the Apostle means only that no one can lead a pious life pleasing to God without faith, confirmed by Enoch's example. Wondrous ingenuity in the Remonstrants, who carved from this their election hanging on foresight of faith.
source_text: Sol. Ad ipsa verba Apostoli primo respondemus, Ea pessime, et in sensum ab instituto Apostolico prorsus alienum, torqueri. Nam fides hoc in loco non praevisam fidem hominis nondum existentis, sed actualem, atque jam vires suas exercentem demonstrat. Hoc perspicuum est ex illo altero verbo εὐηρέστησεν, Placere, quod Apostolus ex Septuaginta Interpretum versione mutuatus est. Sic enim illi Genes. v. 24. εὐηρέστησεν Ἐνὼχ τῷ Θεῷ. At in Hebraeo habetur, continue ambulavit cum Deo: id est, Non est imitatus ejus saeculi nequitiam, sed corde sincero jugiter Deo servivit, Deumque caste coluit. Nihil igitur aliud dicere voluit Apostolus, quam neminem posse absque fide vitam piam Deoque placentem ducere; quod exemplo Enochi voluit confirmare. Miro igitur ingenio sunt Remonstrantes, qui potuerunt electionem suam ex fidei praevisione pendulam hinc exsculpere.
